general.title: Obstruction: a fielder impeding a runner
general.text: Obstruction is a fielder impeding a runner without possessing or legally fielding the ball. Contact is not required. Blocking a runner while waiting for a distant throw can qualify; handling an imminent throw can justify positioning. When a play is being made on the obstructed runner, or the batter-runner is obstructed before first, the ball is dead and that runner receives at least the next base. Otherwise play continues, then the umpire removes the obstruction’s effects; advancing beyond protection risks an out.

general.title: Interference: offense, defense, umpire and spectator
general.text: Offensive interference means the batting team hindering a fielder’s play. A runner must avoid the protected fielder handling a batted ball; interference with a thrown ball requires intent. Offensive interference generally causes a dead ball and an out, subject to exceptions. Defensive interference hinders a batter hitting a pitch, such as catcher’s glove contact with the swing. Umpire and spectator interference are separate categories. The penalty depends on the type and circumstances; interference is not automatically the same ruling as obstruction.

general.title: Fair batted ball bounces over the fence: automatic double
general.text: If a fair batted ball hits the ground and then bounces over the outfield fence, it is an automatic double, commonly called a ground-rule double. The ball is dead. The batter gets second base, and each runner gets two bases from their position at the time of the pitch: a runner on first goes to third; runners on second or third score. A ball clearing the fence without first touching the ground is a different play. USSSA/event modifications and park ground rules take priority; this is the general MLB baseball fallback.

general.title: Infield fly: ordinary effort, runners, outs and youth exceptions
general.text: In standard baseball, a fair fly catchable by an infielder with ordinary effort, with first and second occupied (or bases loaded) and fewer than two outs can be an infield fly. Bunts and line drives do not qualify. The batter is out even if it drops; the ball stays live. Runners advance at their own risk and must retouch after a catch. Coach-pitch, machine-pitch, and younger-division exceptions must be checked before applying this to a game.

eleven.title: pitch tomorrow
eleven.text: An 11U pitcher may throw up to 3 innings in one day and still pitch the next day. Once the pitcher records an out beyond 3 innings (3⅓ or more), the pitcher must rest the next day. Also rest after 8 innings over 2 days or after pitching on 3 straight days.

eleven.title: daily pitching
eleven.text: For 11U, the one-day maximum is 6 innings and the three-consecutive-day maximum is 8 innings. Each out counts as one-third inning. A pitcher recording no outs is charged no innings.

eleven.title: return to pitch
eleven.text: No. Once a player is removed from the pitching position, that player cannot return to pitch during the same game, even though the player may remain at another defensive position.

eleven.title: lead off
eleven.text: The national by-laws add no special 11U restriction on leading off or stealing, so standard baseball rules apply. The restrictions printed in Rule 11 are specifically for 7U and 8U. Always check the event rules for a local modification.

eleven.title: lineup
eleven.text: You may use 9; 9 plus a DH; 10 with an EH; 10 with both DH and EH; or a continuous lineup of every present, eligible, uniformed player. Declare the option before the game and keep it all game.

eleven.title: 8 players
eleven.text: A team may start or continue with 8 eligible players. The ninth batting position is an out each time it comes up. Later arrivals may be added to the bottom.

eleven.title: mercy
eleven.text: For an 11U six-inning game, the national mercy rule is 15 runs beginning in the 3rd inning or 8 runs beginning in the 4th inning.

eleven.title: inning
eleven.text: A regulation 11U game is 6 innings, but it may be shortened by a time limit, mercy rule, weather, or because the home team has already won. The event sets any approved time limit.

eleven.title: field dimensions
eleven.text: The recommended 11U dimensions are 70-foot base paths and a 50-foot pitching distance. Recommended fence distances are 230 feet at the foul lines and 275 feet to center.

eleven.title: fake bunt
eleven.text: Yes. Feinting or faking a bunt and then swinging is allowed for ages 9 and older under the national by-laws. A tournament may publish a stricter event rule, so confirm it.

eleven.title: courtesy runner
eleven.text: A courtesy runner may be used for the pitcher or catcher of record from the previous defensive inning. Use someone not currently in the lineup; if none is available, use the last batted out, subject to the special first-inning procedure.

eleven.title: slide
eleven.text: When a tag play is evident, the runner must slide or seek to avoid contact. Malicious contact can result in an out and ejection. A runner who jumps over a defensive player is out whether contact occurs or not.

eleven.title: age
eleven.text: For 11U, a player who turns 12 before May 1 is ineligible unless in 5th grade. Anyone turning 13 before August 1 is ineligible. An age-eligible 11U player qualifies regardless of grade.

eleven.title: birth certificate
eleven.text: The manager must have a paper or digital copy of each player’s birth certificate available. Grade-exception players also need approved proof of grade. Roster names and dates of birth must exactly match official records.

eleven.title: guest player
eleven.text: From the season start through December 31, teams may use unlimited guest players per event or weekend. From January 1 through season end, the limit is 3. Guest-player classification and roster rules still apply.

eleven.title: protest
eleven.text: National protests are limited to age, pitching violations, or rule interpretations. Declare the protest to the umpire-in-chief and tournament director before the next pitch. The national fee is $100 cash, returned only if upheld.

eleven.title: balk
eleven.text: The 11U national by-laws do not create a balk exception. The no-balk rule is specifically written for 7U and 8U, so standard baseball rules apply at 11U unless the event modifies them.

eleven.title: dropped third
eleven.text: The automatic-out rule on a dropped third strike is specifically for 7U and 8U. At 11U, standard baseball rules apply unless your event publishes a modification.

eleven.title: cleat
eleven.text: 11U players must wear non-metal cleats. Traditional metal spikes begin at 13U under the national rule.

eleven.title: helmet
eleven.text: Batters and runners need double-ear-flap helmets. Catchers need a helmet/mask, built-in or attached throat guard, chest protector, leg guards and protective cup. At 11U, the catcher’s helmet must cover both ears.

eleven.title: concussion
eleven.text: Remove anyone with a suspected concussion or significant blow to the head. They may not return to a USSSA field without written medical clearance from a licensed medical doctor.

eleven.title: time limit
eleven.text: The national by-laws do not set one universal 11U game time. League, qualifier and state events may use an approved time limit, so use the tournament’s supplemental rules.

eleven.title: tie breaker
eleven.text: National pool tiebreakers proceed in order and do not return to an earlier step: winning percentage, wins, losses, head-to-head for two teams, average runs allowed, capped average run differential, USSSA points, database entry date, then coin flip.

eleven.title: coach visit
eleven.text: Two coach visits are allowed per inning. The second visit to the same pitcher in that inning requires a pitching change.
